headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Roo Code can write/egress broadly while the paired profile is non-runnable and non-egressing, making prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks dominated by Roo Code.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Roo Code can read/write workspace files, use MCP, and run browsers, so attacker-controlled content in shared files or MCP outputs can be treated as instructions. The paired profile is a non-runnable collection with no I/O surfaces, so it cannot itself inject back; the interaction risk comes from Roo Code consuming shared workspace content by default.
conditions: IF Roo Code is pointed at a workspace containing untrusted files or MCP output
IF the operator copies content from shared files into Roo Code prompts
mitigations: Restrict Roo Code to a clean workspace
Disable or whitelist MCP servers
Review file contents before opening them in Roo Code
Use separate directories for trusted and untrusted artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Roo Code has broad network egress and handles model-provider API keys, while the paired profile has no data classes touched and no I/O surfaces. Leakage is plausible when Roo Code reads workspace files or screenshots and sends them to configured APIs; the other profile does not add a second leak path, so the risk is driven by Roo Code alone.
conditions: IF Roo Code is configured with a third-party model API
IF sensitive files or screenshots are present in the VS Code workspace
mitigations: Remove secrets from the workspace
Use a local model endpoint
Limit workspace scope to non-sensitive files
Rotate any exposed API keys
Disable screenshot-based workflows for sensitive tasks

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Roo Code can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses, but the paired profile is not runnable and exposes no write surface. There is no meaningful two-way write conflict between the agents; any conflict is one-sided within Roo Code's own workspace, so the pairwise overlap is limited.
conditions: IF the non-runnable profile is replaced by a second writable agent in the same workspace
mitigations: Keep only one writable agent per workspace
Use git branches for each task
Enable per-step approval for file writes
Separate workspaces for parallel sessions

D_cascading_error.rationale: Roo Code can act on browser and filesystem outputs, so if it treats generated content as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into edits or tool actions. The paired profile cannot generate operational outputs because it is non-runnable, so the cascade is not bilateral; however, Roo Code's default action-taking makes single-agent overtrust the relevant pathway.
conditions: IF Roo Code is given unverified text from files or browser pages
IF the operator approves tool actions without manual verification
mitigations: Require human review before tool approval
Cross-check outputs against source files
Disable automatic action chaining
Use a checklist for browser-derived facts

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, HIPAA, or GDPR mismatch is documented for the pair. The only concrete compliance concern is that Roo Code handles model-provider API keys and can send workspace content to configured APIs, while the paired profile has no data handling at all; without a documented cross-agent policy gap, this is a limited operational compliance risk.
conditions: IF sensitive data is placed in the VS Code workspace
IF the configured model provider lacks an approved data-processing agreement
mitigations: Confirm provider retention settings
Avoid placing regulated data in the workspace
Use an approved enterprise endpoint
Document data-handling rules for operators
